name: Pitch
tagline: Turns a prompt or a rough outline into a designed pitch deck you can edit, present, and export.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core trick here, feed a model some context and get back structured slides, is genuinely a weekend build: an LLM call that returns slide JSON, a React renderer, a present mode, done. Where the DIY version falls over is everything after generation. Template design that does not look like a Bootstrap demo is real craft, and an agent will happily produce twelve slides of centered gray text. Export to PPTX or PDF with layout intact is fiddly, and shared links with view tracking mean you now run a server with auth. Fine for personal decks, painful if other people need to open and edit the file.
coreLoopDIY: You paste in company context or a rough outline, an LLM returns a structured slide deck, and you edit, present, and export it as PDF or PPTX from a local app.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Node 20+ and a local SQLite file
Willingness to hand-tune two or three slide templates so they do not look generic
A headless browser dependency if you want good PDF output
whatYouLose: Template libraries that were designed by actual designers, not inferred from a prompt
Real-time collaboration and comments, so co-founder edits go back to sending files around
Reliable PPTX round-tripping for the investor who insists on PowerPoint
Shareable deck links with view analytics, which is the feature people actually brag about
Brand kits, font hosting, and image libraries that keep a deck internally consistent
moatNotes: The defensible part is taste: layout systems that stay readable when the model writes forty words instead of eight.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a pitch deck is a document you show to people who can say no, and nobody wants to explain that the spacing is weird because they built the tool themselves. Paying gets templates that hold up, an export that opens cleanly on someone else's laptop, and a link you can send without hosting anything. The generation step is commodity now; the rest of the product is why it still has customers.
notes: The generator is easy, the typography is not, and the typography is what the deck is judged on.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI pitch deck tool in an empty folder. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud storage.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite via better-sqlite3, and the OpenAI SDK. Everything runs with `npm run dev` on localhost.

Core loop:
1. A single page form where I paste raw context: company, problem, product, market, traction, ask. Plus a dropdown for deck type: fundraising, sales, internal update.
2. POST that to /api/generate, which calls the LLM with a strict JSON schema and returns an array of slides. Each slide: { layout, title, subtitle, bullets[], bodyText, notes }.
3. Allowed layouts, and only these: title, statement, bullets, two-column, metrics (three big numbers with labels), quote, closing. Reject or repair any model output that uses another layout.
4. Persist decks and slides to SQLite. List saved decks on the home page.

Editor: a left rail of slide thumbnails, a center canvas rendering the real slide at 16:9, and a right panel of plain text inputs bound to the current slide's fields. Edits save on blur. Support add slide, delete slide, and drag to reorder.

Rendering: build the slide layouts as React components using a fixed 1280x720 design frame scaled with CSS transform, so the canvas, present mode, and export all use the exact same markup. Define a small design token file: two fonts, one accent color, a type scale, consistent margins. Do not center everything. Left align body text.

Present mode: /present/[deckId] renders fullscreen, arrow keys and space to advance, `s` toggles speaker notes on a second window.

Export: /api/export/[deckId] uses Playwright to print the present route to a PDF at exact 16:9 page size. PDF only.

Out of scope, do not build: PPTX export, image generation, sharing links, view analytics, multi-user anything, charts beyond the metrics layout.

Put OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.local and read it server side only. Write a README with setup, the three commands I need, and a short note on where to edit the design tokens.
